detail: Full summary: the calibrated table leaves ascii_space at the PROVEN ratio 1.0 because whitespace.txt is the one corpus doc the count-tokens API refuses (blank text), so the calibrate script skips it and no document is dominated by that class. Whitespace is ~15% of briefing bytes, so this alone costs ~0.15 tokens/byte of the residual looseness — measured prose density is 0.42-0.44 rather than the ~0.28 a fully-measured table would give. ascii_punct is also 1.0, but there by clamp (measured x 1.15 exceeded the proven bound), which is correct. To close the space gap the corpus needs a document that is >=80% whitespace bytes yet not blank — e.g. indented/padded text — since a document the API will actually count is the only way that class gets a measurement.
